title.value: Adaptation, Comparison and Practical Implementation of Fairness Schemes in Kidney Exchange Programs
title.justification: The paper explicitly discusses the implementation and comparison of fairness schemes in the context of kidney exchange programs (KEPs).
title.quote: Adaptation, Comparison and Practical Implementation of Fairness Schemes in Kidney Exchange Programs

extractions.description: The paper explores fairness schemes in Kidney Exchange Programs (KEPs) to balance individual patient benefits with the utilitarian goal of maximizing transplants. It adapts popular fairness concepts and compares different schemes via conic programs and column generation approaches. The study analyzes the efficiency and effectiveness of the fairness procedures in achieving a balance between utility and fairness in practical KEP scenarios.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The study focuses on fairness in kidney exchange programs, which is a healthcare and ethical issue rather than a climate or ecological sustainability one.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In this work, we seek instead to find a policy that contemplates the probability of patients of being in a solution. To guide the determination of our policy, we adapt popular fairness schemes to KEPs to balance the usual approach of maximizing the utilitarian objective.

primary_category.justification: The paper's focus is on healthcare and ethics related to kidney exchange programs rather than climate or ecological sustainability.
primary_category.quote: The primary objective of KEPs is to find a solution, namely an exchange plan that consists of a set of donor exchanges resulting in compatible transplants for the patients.

secondary_categories.quote: Several approaches to fairness in KEPs have been explored.

applications.value: Balancing fairness and utility in kidney exchange programs
applications.justification: The paper focuses on implementing fairness schemes in kidney exchange programs, which is a specific application area mentioned throughout the paper.
applications.quote: We aim to compare fairness schemes driven by a single-objective (a fairness score) and fairness schemes based on multi-objective models, which we refer to as the Social Welfare Program and the Nash Social Welfare Program.
